acceptance_status: Automated-inventory checkpoint; full functional/native/manual/performance/release parity remains open.
scope: History result text/backing uses Rust recipes on the existing shared tools Metal underlay, with no per-row drawable or Label children. History list placement uses the Rust column layout. Native event/focus/AX nodes and profile-bound navigation callbacks remain adapters.

build_input_snapshot.gn_delta: No target/dependency change. Rust bridge adds clear_selection for existing SelectState. Explicit native adapters, preference selector allocation/refresh and browser tests changed. Concurrent root network-policy work remains excluded.
build_input_snapshot.method: Frozen UI overlay base a3afc206f742f0a59da6e65d609ddf1df3c7326d plus 16 explicit live UI overrides (including sidebar_metal.h/mm), with committed own installer/stager hooks; concurrent network-policy changes excluded. Twenty-one prototype source hashes are matched to committed, live and staged inputs.

native_service_patch.license: Generated Chromium header and source hook retain the Chromium BSD-style license; project adapter/tool/model changes use Apache-2.0.

contracts: SceneHistoryRow reuses the existing Rust RowPointer reducer and native Button/focus/AX adapter. Its title and date/URL detail become display-only Rust scene data; the native callback still captures the actual GURL/current profile, posts navigation, checks profile identity, opens a new tab and restores page focus. Views retains its original RowButton/Label/BoxLayout hierarchy.

One existing transparent tools underlay renders only projected visible history rows. The collector recognizes migrated rows before the general native Button cutout rule; editor/selector/action/dismiss controls remain holes. No new per-row Metal drawable or native Label is created. CPU fallback consumes the same Rust recipe, retaining per-primitive font sizes, title/detail elision and focus drawing while the shared underlay is absent.

A new history-row recipe keeps the native 60px row height, 36px text lead, 10px trailing space, primary column capped at 3/5 of available width, native measured title width, 10px column gap, tail primary elision and middle date/URL elision. Native Unicode/font/time-format services provide display data/metrics. Rust column layout preserves 4px spacing and full scroll extent.

Visible bounds, paint/input, theme and bounds changes schedule the shared renderer. Explicit scroll synchronization cancels fully offscreen pending input; mouse/key release also checks actual row/window visibility. Fully hidden rows cancel pending Rust input; widget hide cancels rows before hiding the underlay. Rebuilt result lists explicitly schedule rendering, including empty lists. Full profile/query/limit service admission remains as in the preceding ToolsForm checkpoint.

The new shared browser test seeds real service history, checks Unicode and empty-title URL fallback, AX name/description, childlessness versus the original Labels, row/list geometry and real Cocoa Space activation followed by the expected new-tab URL. A dedicated Metal case seeds 80 rows and checks actual scene text/order/cutouts, viewport culling, scrolling, offscreen/hide press cancellation, reconstruction, dark theme and profile isolation.

The earlier shared-chrome test now requires history row text in the scene and no row Label children, instead of the former native result-row hole. Its other underlay/control/text/error requirements remain. Existing history pagination/search/clear, tools controller, preferences and other browser-service tests remain covered.

No new crate/library/dependency, browser store or service authority is introduced. Remaining native interaction/list/window ownership is not considered migrated merely because presentation moved to Metal.
initial_compile_issue: Chromium BindRepeating rejects WeakPtr-bound methods returning bool. The visibility callback now uses a lambda that explicitly checks the weak owner and returns false after destruction; the initial failed build log is retained.

initial_probe.resolution: The initial Metal probe exposed offscreen press/release navigation. Explicit scroll synchronization and release visibility checks now cancel it, preserving the no-navigation assertion. Native focus rings were disabled only for migrated rows because Rust owns their focus primitive; CPU fallback uses the same recipe with font/elision. The initial shared test also incorrectly assumed title-based AX names and exactly two native children: both backends preserve Chromium tooltip-URL AX naming, while Views retains two Labels plus its focus-ring node. Final tests verify URL naming, native Label contents and complete migrated childlessness.

optional_scenarios.status: Not rerun for this presentation checkpoint. The earlier tools-chrome report retains four default-30-trial passes per backend; none is counted as a current-commit pass.

limits: Tools action/status decisions, provider/shortcut editing coordination, busy state, other form/service panels and outer/native interaction/container ownership remain. History presentation and column placement are Rust/Metal, but native row Button/event/focus/AX, View groups and scrolling remain adapters. Stores/confirmations/service operations stay native.
Manual IME/candidate-window, VoiceOver, complex bidi/RTL, typography/scale, pointer/trackpad, detach/reattach and GPU recovery acceptance remain open.
No controlled CPU/GPU/drawable-presentation speedup or memory improvement is claimed.
Normal installed applications/profiles were untouched; no release bundle was packaged/signed. Final shipped-binary Apache-2.0/upstream license/notice acceptance remains open.
